items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: The Nifty index fell for a third straight day, closing lower amid rising market volatility. Analysts suggest markets may face continued pressure due to oil prices and bond yields. Foreign portfolio investors and domestic institutional investors were net buyers of shares on Wednesday. The Indian rupee ended little changed, supported by the Reserve Bank of India. SAIL and LIC Housing Finance are currently in the F&O ban period.

items.title: Stocks in news: Swiggy, Adani Ports, IDFC First Bank, Hexaware Technologies and Sun Pharma
items.description: Indian markets experienced a sharp decline on Wednesday due to global factors.  Technical analysis suggests further downside potential for the Nifty index.  Several companies like Swiggy and Adani Ports are in focus today.  Hyundai Motor India aims to regain its market position with new launches.  ONGC is reviewing its Venezuelan assets after receiving US approval.

items.title: Zerodha unit gets nod for merchant banking
items.description: On September 1, Zerodha Corporate Advisors secured approval from Sebi to function as a merchant banker, following their application back in April. This pivotal approval enables the firm to facilitate initial public offerings and handle various capital market activities. Although the complete registration process with the regulator remains in progress, Zerodha Corporate Advisors is gearing up to launch its new merchant banking services shortly.

items.title: Small finance banks' asset quality to improve, GNPA to drop by 120 basis points by March 2027: Crisil
items.description: Small finance banks anticipate improved asset quality this financial year.  Gross non-performing assets are projected to decline significantly by March 2027.  This improvement stems from microfinance portfolio recovery and stable non-microfinance growth.  Tighter underwriting practices have strengthened borrower selection in microfinance portfolios.  Borrower over-indebtedness caused past credit stress in microfinance books.

items.title: Insurers plan floor for fire cover to avoid large burns
items.description: Non-life insurers are considering a minimum rate for fire insurance's natural catastrophe component. This move follows concerns about steep discounts exposing the industry and reinsurers to losses. The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India chairman also expressed worries about insurer financial health. Aggressive pricing and recent fire losses in Gujarat have fueled these discussions. Insurers aim to restrict discounts to the flexible fire rate component.

items.title: 'Revolver' misfire hits credit card issuers: India's credit card boom sees lower bank profits
items.description: Credit card profits are shrinking for Indian banks as spending rises. Customers now use cards more for payments than borrowing, reducing interest income. Interest-bearing balances have significantly fallen as a percentage of total card spending. This trend is impacting major lenders like HDFC Bank and SBI Cards. Analysts predict further profit margin declines in the coming years.

items.title: FIIs are showering India with billions. Why are Nifty stocks missing the party?
items.description: Despite foreign investors infusing billions into Indian equities, benchmark indices struggle to keep pace. Inflows in the primary market are notable but fail to directly uplift listed stocks. Selective purchases are occurring in large mid-cap stocks while financials and IT remain ignored. Domestic investors are a crucial pillar for market resilience, necessitating consistent secondary market activity for a comprehensive rally.

items.title: Sensex rises over 300 points, Nifty near 24,000 as US bonds yields slightly ease. Why is caution still warranted?
items.description: Indian stock markets traded higher on Thursday, with key indices showing gains. The Sensex rose over 300 points, reaching 76,900 on its weekly expiry day. Nifty 50 also gained over 83 points, beginning the session near 23,998. Broader markets followed suit, with midcap and smallcap indices experiencing upward movement. This positive start occurred after a significant decline in the previous trading session.

items.title: Power Grid shares gain 1.5% after firm wins Rs 3,244 crore inter-state transmission system project. Should you buy?
items.description: Shares of Power Grid experienced an uptick after the company secured an important transmission project aimed at facilitating power evacuation from Rajasthan. This endeavor will incorporate the establishment of HVDC terminals and a long-distance transmission line. Power Grid's successful bid for this vital project reflects its strategic growth, amidst varying stock performance observed in recent months.

items.title: Persistent Systems shares fall over 3% as board gives nod for $1.25 billion fundraise. Check details
items.description: Persistent Systems approved plans to raise up to $1.25 billion through debt and up to $450 million via equity-linked instruments, subject to approvals. The IT firm reported strong bookings and revenue growth in Q1, though profit declined due to forex losses. Shares have gained 21% over six months.

items.title: Swiggy shares fall 2%, down for 3rd session, as MSCI set to remove stock from Global Standard Indexes from September 7
items.description: Shares of Swiggy experienced a decline following MSCI's decision to exclude the company from global indexes, prompted by its shift to full Indian ownership and control. The new foreign ownership constraints limit further investments. Swiggy is targeting robust adjusted EBITDA growth by FY31, even as it reported a net loss while revenues showed an uptick in Q1 FY27.

items.title: Kwick Forensic Solutions shares debut at 67% premium over IPO price on BSE SME platform
items.description: The IPO, which opened for subscription on August 27 and closed on August 31, witnessed an extraordinary response from investors, with the issue subscribed a staggering 289 times overall.

items.title: Lumino Industries shares list at 34% premium over IPO price
items.description: The Rs 700-crore IPO was offered in a price band of Rs 78–Rs 82 per share. The issue comprised a fresh issue of Rs 500 crore, involving 6.10 crore shares, and an offer for sale (OFS) of Rs 200 crore, involving 2.44 crore shares sold by promoters Devendra Goel and Jay Goel.

items.title: Hitachi Energy emerges as potential ‘buy’ on strong order inflows, earnings visibility
items.description: Hitachi Energy shares have surged significantly this year on robust revenue growth.  The company secured new orders for battery storage and data centers.  Its substantial order book provides a strong near-term earnings driver.  Future growth is anticipated from high-voltage direct current projects and capacity expansion.  Analysts have revised price targets upwards, reflecting strong future prospects.

items.title: Happiest Minds shares fall for 5th day as merger concerns weigh
items.description: The stock of Happiest Minds Technologies has experienced a significant downturn due to uncertainty related to the ITC Infotech integration. Promoters will cash in, whereas minority shareholders are set to receive shares in the merger. The merger is expected to enhance long-term profitability. Yet, HDFC Securities has downgraded the stock, pointing out the lack of a takeover premium and the anticipated integration time.

items.title: MSCI to drop Swiggy from global indices on September 7
items.description: Global index providers MSCI and FTSE are set to revise Swiggy's index treatment shortly. MSCI is removing Swiggy from global indices, which will lead to considerable passive outflows. Additionally, FTSE has modified Swiggy's investability weight due to foreign ownership limits. Together, these alterations are projected to trigger passive outflows surpassing $350 million, causing Swiggy shares to drop on Wednesday after the news broke.

items.title: Investing beyond Trump, oil prices and bond yields: 5 large-caps from different sectors with upside potential of up to 17%
items.description: The US-Iran war is escalating once again. And as Brent crude went past $91 a barrel, Indian equities have come under pressure; the war is clearly dictating the mood on Dalal Street. The question investors are asking is the same one they ask every time the Gulf erupts: How long will this last? No one knows. It could end tomorrow, or in a few weeks. It could also stretch well beyond what the markets currently expect.

items.title: Aswath Damodaran disagrees with Vinod Khosla on the scaling vs profitability debate. Here’s why
items.description: Aswath Damodaran has challenged Vinod Khosla’s view that companies should prioritise scaling over profitability. Damodaran argues that the right balance depends on factors such as market size, competition, capital intensity and unit economics. He warns that blindly chasing scale can turn small business failures into larger ones and create unsustainable models.

items.title: PTC India, Coal India among 10 stocks offering dividend yields of up to 10%
items.description: High-dividend-yield stocks remain on investors’ radar for their potential to generate regular income. According to a September report by Religare Broking, these 10 companies across power, mining, finance, IT and energy offered dividend yields ranging from 3.3% to 9.7%.

items.title: Supreme Court dismisses Sebi’s plea against NSE: Report
items.description: In a pivotal ruling, India's supreme court has dismissed the regulatory challenges raised by market authorities against the National Stock Exchange. This verdict eliminates a major hurdle for the exchange's initial public offering, addressing previous controversies over co-location and dark fibre allegations. CNBC TV-18 provided coverage of this significant development on Thursday, paving the way for the IPO to proceed.

items.title: Bonus issue alert! Multibagger Titan Biotech announces its maiden 1:4 bonus issue
items.description: Titan Biotech has announced its maiden 1:4 bonus issue, with one share to be issued for every four held, subject to shareholder approval. The multibagger stock has gained over 200% in a year and 100% in 2026. Here’s what investors need to know about the bonus issue and eligibility.

items.title: Wakefit shares jump over 4% as Nomura initiates coverage. Check target price
items.description: Wakefit Innovations shares gained over 4% after Nomura initiated coverage with a Buy rating and a Rs 200 target price, implying 30.7% upside. The brokerage cited Wakefit’s leadership in online mattresses, furniture expansion and vertically integrated model, while flagging Jumbo store execution, competition and raw-material volatility as key risks.

items.title: Motilal Oswal initiates coverage on Adani Power with Buy call, sees 20% upside. Time to hold or sell?
items.description: Motilal Oswal initiated coverage on Adani Power with a Buy rating and a target price of Rs 250, implying around 20% upside. The brokerage sees capacity expansion, its track record of turning around distressed assets and potential entry into nuclear power as key growth drivers.

items.title: Lumino Industries shares soar 40% from IPO price after strong market debut. Should you buy or wait?
items.description: Lumino Industries shares extended their strong debut gains, rising another 4% after listing at a 34% premium to the IPO price. While analysts see attractive valuations, strong profitability and debt reduction as positives, fresh investors have been advised to wait for consolidation, while IPO allottees can consider partial profit booking and monitor key support levels.

items.title: Madhusudan Kela’s portfolio: Top 5 holdings and how they performed in August
items.description: Market veteran Madhusudan Kela is closely tracked for his stock picks. He publicly holds around 19 stocks worth nearly Rs 2,568 crore, according to Trendlyne data. Here are his top five holdings and their performance in August.

items.title: Nominal GDP growth set to surge to 12%. Why the stock market may still struggle to rally
items.description: India’s nominal GDP growth could accelerate to 11.5%-12% in FY27, supporting stronger corporate earnings. However, elevated valuations, rising equity supply and potentially slower domestic flows could limit broad market gains. Jefferies favours lenders, power, ports and real estate, but sees a selective stock-picking environment rather than a broad-based rally.

items.title: IFCI shares rally over 16% in two days as NSE IPO draws closer
items.description: IFCI shares rallied over 16% in two sessions amid expectations that the long-delayed NSE IPO could be nearing launch. IFCI indirectly owns more than 4% of NSE through its stake in Stock Holding Corporation of India. SEBI has moved closer to approving NSE’s IPO after settling key regulatory cases, while the exchange seeks a valuation of up to Rs 5.26 lakh crore.

items.title: HUDCO shares jump 4% after signing Rs 25,000 crore MoU with Bihar government for infrastructure development
items.description: HUDCO shares jumped nearly 4% after the company signed an MoU with the Government of Bihar to provide financial assistance of up to Rs 25,000 crore over five years for industrial infrastructure and land acquisition. The development comes after HUDCO signed another Rs 1 lakh crore MoU with Bihar in July for urban infrastructure projects.

items.title: F&O Radar: Call Ratio Spread strategy for RBL Bank this week
items.description: RBL Bank has broken out of a consolidation zone, with technical indicators pointing to improving momentum and a sustained bullish trend. The stock has found support near its 50-day EMA and moved above its 20-day EMA. Here’s a Call Ratio Spread strategy for RBL Bank, with Rs 400 as the potential upside target.

items.title: 5 smallcap stocks with upside potential of up to 32%. How many do you have?
items.description: Axis Securities has raised its December 2026 Nifty target to 27,360 as it remains constructive on Indian equities, supported by strong macroeconomic fundamentals, sustained government capital expenditure, GST 2.0 reforms and an improving corporate earnings cycle. Axis expects Nifty earnings to grow at a 13% CAGR over FY23-FY28, which it believes will underpin healthy medium-term market returns. Here are five small- and midcap stocks that the brokerage is bullish on.

items.title: Explained: What $127 billion FCNR(B) inflows mean for ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank, other bank stocks
items.description: Closing the FCNR(B) scheme has led to a noteworthy increase in dollar inflows, which has positively impacted foreign exchange reserves. Indian banks have benefited from these substantial funds, assisting in the continued growth of loans. Nonetheless, the Reserve Bank of India must now tackle the critical issue of managing surplus liquidity efficiently.

items.title: Welspun Corp shares jump 6% after Jefferies initiates coverage with Buy rating. Should you invest?
items.description: Welspun Corp shares jumped nearly 6% after Jefferies initiated coverage with a Buy rating and a Rs 3,250 target price, implying 27% upside. The brokerage sees a multi-year upcycle in US and Saudi energy infrastructure spending, supported by Welspun’s capacity expansion, strong order book and growing overseas operations.

items.title: Weekly Top Picks: These stocks scored 10 on 10 on Stock Reports Plus
items.description: Stock Reports Plus, powered by Refinitiv, undertakes detailed company analysis for 4,000+ listed stocks. In addition to detailed company analyses, the report also collates analysts’ forecasts and trend analysis for each component. An average score in Stock Reports Plus is calculated by undertaking quantitative analysis of five key investment tools – earnings, fundamentals, relative valuation, risk, and price momentum.

items.title: India bonds pare gains as oil spike tames FCNR boost
items.description: Early Thursday trading saw Indian government bonds lose their initial gains as stronger dollar inflows were overshadowed by soaring oil prices. Traders covering short positions led to better performance in shorter maturities. Abundant liquidity helped reduce overnight indexed swap rates, but the spike in oil prices heightened concerns about India's inflation trajectory and fiscal integrity.

items.title: CAS chaos returns: Sensex puts explode up to 400% as fag-end slide jolts traders
items.description: Sensex experienced a sharp 2,100-point drop during the closing auction session on expiry day, causing a massive surge in out-of-the-money put options. This volatility highlights ongoing concerns about the closing auction session’s impact on index derivatives pricing.

items.title: Market wrap: Adani Ports, Axis Bank, Tech Mahindra, Bajaj Auto top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Thursday
items.description: Indian markets extended losses on Thursday, with the Sensex falling nearly 0.6% and the Nifty declining 0.17% as geopolitical tensions and elevated crude prices weighed on sentiment. Realty stocks outperformed, while IT stocks lagged. Here’s a look at the top Nifty and Sensex gainers and losers, along with the technical outlook.

items.title: When Nithin faked being Sachin: Kamath looks back on using a pseudonym in early years of Zerodha
items.description: Zerodha founder Nithin Kamath recalled how a 15-year-old media appearance helped boost the broker’s account openings in its early days. He also revealed that he used the pseudonym “Sachin” and even faked an accent while speaking to a journalist. Kamath later turned to social media as traditional media’s influence waned.

items.title: NSE's unlisted shares down 17% from peak ahead of IPO; BSE falls 29%. Which is a better bet right now?
items.description: NSE is inching closer to its much-awaited IPO as SEBI nears approval of its DRHP. While unlisted NSE shares remain 17% below their peak, BSE has corrected nearly 29% from its 52-week high. Experts compare the two exchanges on valuations, earnings, liquidity and growth prospects to assess which offers better value.

items.title: Up to 290% gains! SBI, Federal Bank make massive windfall as Arcil’s Rs 733-crore IPO hits D-Street
items.description: SBI and Federal Bank have gained 281% and 292%, respectively, on Arcil investments as the asset reconstruction company launches its Rs 733-crore IPO. The entirely OFS issue opens September 9, with Arcil reporting stronger FY26 profit and revenue growth overall.

items.title: Beyond Stocks and Bonds: Rethinking wealth creation with alternative assets
items.description: ET Alpha Summit 2.0 will bring together leading investment voices to explore how niche alternative assets could shape the next phase of multi-generational wealth creation. The masterclass will examine emerging opportunities, onshoring trends and structural shifts, while weighing return potential against risk, complexity and liquidity.

items.title: Jindal Worldwide shares jump 20% to hit upper circuit, up 66% in 2026; check what’s driving the rally
items.description: Jindal Worldwide shares hit a 52-week high and upper circuit after subsidiary Jindal Mobilitric announced plans to expand its retail network to around 100 showrooms by FY28. The EV expansion has driven strong investor interest, with shares gaining 66.28% year-to-date.

items.title: Sensex falls 417 points, Nifty closes below 23,900 as market erases all morning gains. What lies ahead?
items.description: Indian stock markets faced a downturn on Thursday, marking a continuation of prior losses. Both the Sensex and Nifty slipped, largely influenced by the fluctuations in oil prices and bond yields. Major corporations like Titan and ITC reported notable share price declines. Contrarily, the broader market displayed resilience, as small and midcap indices flourished, leading to a favorable market breadth on the NSE.

items.title: Calcutta exchange’s unlisted shares double on revival hopes
items.description: Calcutta Stock Exchange shares have more than doubled in the unlisted market in three months as hopes of a revival gain momentum. The exchange is seeking to pause its voluntary exit process and explore opportunities across equities, derivatives, bonds, currencies and commodities, though any revival will require regulatory approvals and potential anchor investors.

items.title: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Friday
items.description: The Indian stock market closed lower Thursday, with Sensex down 417 points and Nifty falling 41 points, pressured by high oil prices, bond yields, and geopolitical tensions. Despite strong domestic growth, near-term market direction hinges on global risks and crude oil volatility.

items.title: Sebi to review derivatives settlement price methodology after CAS volatility
items.description: Sebi will review derivative settlement prices after market feedback.  The Closing Auction Session's impact on expiry-day settlement is a concern.  Traders reported sudden option price swings during the auction window.  This review follows the equity cash segment's Closing Auction Session introduction.  A consultation paper on proposed changes will be issued soon.

items.title: Gland Pharma shares: Promoter Fosun Pharma likely to divest 5% equity worth Rs 2,279 crore via block deal
items.description: Fosun Pharma plans to divest 5% equity in Gland Pharma through a Rs 2,279.5 crore block deal at Rs 2,763 per share. Gland Pharma reported a 47% rise in Q1FY27 profit and operates globally, with strong R&D and growth.

items.title: Two Trades for Today: 2 PSU banks; one a mid-cap for an 8.4% gain, the other a large-cap for a rise of 6%
items.description: Our technical analysts identify select stocks every trading day that may gain momentum even in volatile markets. Here are the technical calls for today.

items.title: FCNRB deposits: Why bank investors should watch RoE, not just NIM
items.description: FCNR(B) deposits could boost banks’ return on equity despite a mild impact on net interest margins, according to Anand Rathi. Exemptions from reserve requirements, capital-efficient lending and longer tenors could improve returns. The brokerage analysed four scenarios, including deposit costs, leverage and rising rates, to assess the scheme’s benefits.
